title: Land the durable environment-retirement record (leaf)
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-de80c663569a4ab2b30a9db6ac526e4b ("an environment can never be retired, so the health sweep probes dead URLs forever"), split by architect-5385678f 2026-09-08 because the parent's full shape touches 19 non-.moe files and moe.submit_plan hard-rejects past 10.

OBJECTIVE. Land the durable, replayable FACT that an environment is retired. Nothing reads it and nothing writes it yet — those are children 2 and 4.

DELIVERABLE WHEN DONE: a new `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/environment-retirement-record.ts` exporting a `createEnvironmentRetirementRecord({ store, projectId, now })` whose shape mirrors `createProbeIntervalRecord` in the sibling file `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/probe-interval-record.ts` — READ IT FIRST AND FOLLOW IT. That module is the exact precedent for "a durable fact layered over the append-only deploy ledger", it already owns its name grammar and its FIXED refusal codes, and it already exposes both a per-name read and a `stored()` snapshot the sweep can consult per tick. Do not invent a second persistence idiom.

WHAT THE RECORD MUST GUARANTEE:
- DURABLE AND REPLAYABLE, never in-memory: the fact is an event in the store and survives a daemon restart. This is the parent's DoD 2 and it is the reason this row exists as a leaf.
- THE DEPLOY LEDGER STAYS APPEND-ONLY (parent DoD 3). Retirement is layered OVER `readDeployLedger`, never a receipt deletion and never a mutation of a receipt.
- HISTORY SURVIVES (parent DoD 3): a retired environment's probe ring and deploy receipts stay readable exactly as before. Assert that, do not assume it.
- Retiring an unknown environment, or an invalid name, refuses with a stable code and layer — follow the sibling's fixed-code convention rather than inventing free text.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: no command kind, no registry wiring, no vocabulary or digest-mirror change (child 3), no daemon command edge (child 4), and NO change to the sweep (child 2). This row adds a module and its arms; the health sweep still enumerates every ledger environment when it lands, which is correct and expected.

CONSUMER EDGE (global rail 4 clause 1): this leaf's consumer is child 2, which is declared dependsOn this row. It is not left uncomposed.

VERIFICATION COMMAND: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — run it FOREGROUND and STANDALONE and quote the `Test Files N passed` count line, not just the exit code (a `--filter` leg that matches no package also exits 0).
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/src/monitoring/environment-retirement-record.ts exists and exports a record factory whose read/stored surface mirrors createProbeIntervalRecord in probe-interval-record.ts.
Retirement survives a restart: an arm reconstructs the record from a reopened store and reads the retired name back, proving the fact is durable rather than in-memory.
The deploy ledger is untouched: an arm asserts readDeployLedger still returns the retired environment and its receipts after retirement, and no receipt is deleted or mutated.
A retired environment's probe ring stays readable: an arm reads its existing samples back after retirement.
An invalid or unknown environment name refuses with a stable code AND layer, asserted by both, following the sibling record's fixed-code convention.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description: TDD: add real-store regression arms in environment-retirement-record.test.ts before implementing the module; load test-driven-development. Seed actual deploy receipts using recordDeployReceipt and actual sidecar samples using createHealthProbeRing, not a mock ledger. Pin planned public shapes with deep equality: read(valid unset/unknown) -> {ok:true,value:false}, stored() -> empty Map, write(known) -> {ok:true,value:true}. Cover durable true after close/reopen; two record instances observe fresh state; repeat retirement appends no second event; mutation of a returned Map cannot affect later reads; environment/project isolation. Compare readDeployLedger's whole environment state and readDeployReceipt resultBytes before/after retirement and reopening, plus complete ring sample arrays, proving history unchanged. Generation arms: failed deployment and replayed success leave retirement true; new DEPLOYED receipt with the SAME SHA clears effective retirement in read AND stored; re-retirement persists the new generation; an environment with only REFUSED receipts can retire with a null successful cutoff and its first success reactivates it. Inject invalid name/unknown write, malformed durable event (invalid JSON/schema/version/type or cutoff not a successful receipt belonging to that environment), readEvents/readCommandDecisionsAfter/commit exceptions and expectedVersion conflict; assert exact code AND layer DAEMON_INGRESS on every failure and no new retirement event on rejected writes. Codes: ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_ENVIRONMENT_INVALID, ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN, ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_RECORD_INVALID, ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_STORE_FAILED. Invalid names refuse before any store call. Use real store with a bound delegating Proxy only for fault injection, assert the injected seam was actually reached. Use try/finally from immediately after mkdtemp through setup/assertion failure and reopen: close every store first, then delete only the resolved exact created directory after verifying it is a child of the intended temp root; native Node paths work on Windows/macOS/Linux. No secret fixtures, arbitrary old-temp cleanup, server, container or schedule. Capture the initial red as TDD evidence rather than claiming an import error is behavioral proof; final drills will pin behavior.

implementationPlan.description: Implement only environment-retirement-record.ts and its exact LF bridge `export * from "./environment-retirement-record.ts";\n`. Export factory createEnvironmentRetirementRecord({store:SqliteEventStore,projectId,now?}), types EnvironmentRetirementRecord/Result/Code/Config, with read(environment):Result<boolean>, stored():Result<ReadonlyMap<string,true>>, write(environment):Result<true>. The existing @moe/store bare-import edge is verified in planningNotes/comment-221f307; no dependency edits. Reuse admitEnvironmentName and readDeployLedger through local .js imports; no producer edits. Match frozen result/record and fresh project-scoped replay idiom of probe-interval-record, but keep replay version local to each operation. NEW isolated aggregate `environment-retirement/${projectId}`, event type `moe.environment.retired`, strict JSON payload with exactly {version:1,environment,retiredThroughReceiptId:string|null}. Non-null cutoff must identify a DEPLOYED receipt in that same project's environment ledger. Decode malformed payload/schema/version/event type/invalid reference as ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_RECORD_INVALID; exceptions in store reads/commit, CAS conflicts or clock conversion become ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_STORE_FAILED, always fixed code+DAEMON_INGRESS without exception text. Invalid input name gets ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_ENVIRONMENT_INVALID before IO. Unknown WRITE gets ENVIRONMENT_RETIREMENT_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN and performs no append; valid unknown READ defaults false when replay is healthy. Replay latest retirement per environment, load deploy ledger once per operation, and expose only effectively retired names: compare cutoff with latest DEPLOYED receiptId in ledger order (null if no success). Do not use timestamps, SHA or a REFUSED current receipt for reactivation. Every read/stored call derives fresh state; caller Map mutation cannot poison subsequent calls. Write captures current successful cutoff; already effectively retired is an idempotent true with no append; otherwise commit one retirement event using expectedVersion from this replay, fresh UUID command/event IDs, payload as commandBytes, injected now/Date.now for committedAt. Do not cache or return success after failed append. A later successful generation ends effective retirement, without deleting any retirement event, receipt or sample; re-retire appends the new cutoff. Explain these effective-vs-historical and observed-generation concurrency semantics in concise API comments. No explicit unretire operation or authority/sweep wiring in this leaf.

planningNotes.risks: A retirement applies to the successful receipt generation observed by write, not to any later successful deployment; do not claim atomic ordering across deployment and retirement aggregates. Refused attempts and decision replay must not reactivate. A corrupted record or unavailable ledger must return its exact refusal, never manufacture an authoritative retired or active snapshot. Existing SqliteEventStore is non-extensible: failure injection uses a delegating Proxy with original methods bound, not spyOn. Close every opened store before owned mkdtemp teardown; HealthProbeRing closes per-operation connections and has no close method. Only these three paths are owned; preserve all peer WIP. Target production <=250 physical lines, split before400 through amendment, never silently take a fourth path. No standing-preview provisioning or real deploy/container/probe schedule in this leaf. Broad-lane reds must be path-attributed and disclosed, not hidden by reruns.
